patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Linear and Microsoft Project share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Linear and Microsoft Project share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Linear only if your buying job matches “Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo ” rather than Microsoft Project's shape. Choose Microsoft Project only if your buying job matches “Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan ” rather than Linear's shape. Workflow advantage: Linear leans shared coverage; Microsoft Project leans resource-planning, timeline-reporting. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Linear and Microsoft Project share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Linear is Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo annual.; Microsoft Project is Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan 1 from ~$10/user/mo..
- Company-size focus: Linear (startup, small-business, mid-market) vs Microsoft Project (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Linear-leaning — vs Microsoft Project-leaning resource-planning, timeline-reporting.
- Researched limits: Linear — Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Microsoft Project — SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans.

Limitations — Linear: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Leaner automation than Jira Enterprise; Microsoft Project: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Best value assumes Microsoft 365 standardisation.

Poor-fit cases: Linear is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS · Microsoft Project is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans · Avoid Linear if you actually need Microsoft Project's motion (Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Pla)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
